newsitem.title: USA: U.S stocks set more records, aided by techs, banks.
newsitem.headline: U.S stocks set more records, aided by techs, banks.

text.p: U.S. stocks shattered more records on Wall Street, aided by renewed vigor in technology and follow-though buying in financial issues and other blue chips.

"The market keeps chugging ahead. The driving force is the market has been basically moving higher every year for six years, and it's fairly magnetic to investors," said Gail Dudack, chief investment strategist at UBS Securities.
The Dow industrials rose 29 to about 5934, topping the previous record close of 5904.90 set Tuesday.
After closing above 5900 for the first time Tuesday, "we're reaching for the 6000 mark. At this rate, we can get there by the end of the week," said Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage.
The S&P 500 notched its third consecutive all-time high finish, up five to about 694. The NYSE Composite posted its fifth straight record, up two to about 371.
The tech-rich Nasdaq Composite, which shed 8.54 points over the past two sessions, rallied 15 to about 1236. That drew the index ever closer to the record closing high of 1249.15, set June 5.
Winners beat losers 16-7 on heavy NYSE volume of about 437 million shares.
Stocks were supported by continued strength in the Treasuries market. The long bond rose 15/32, knocking its yield down to 6.84 percent, the lowest since August 22.

Stronger technology issues included IBM, up 2-1/4 to 125-3/4, BMC Software, up 6-3/4 to 86-1/2, and Intel, up 3-1/4 to 99. Among financial stocks, Citicorp rose 7/8 to 92-3/8 after reaching a year-high 92-7/8. Chase Manhattan added 1/4 to 80-3/4 after touching a 52-week high 81-3/8, and Sallie Mae gained 4-3/4 to 83-1/4.
Wall Street took Wednesday's only economic release in stride. August U.S. construction spending rose 0.9 percent, a shade higher than the expected 0.8 percent increase.

Investors are being lured to stocks by a growing conviction that the long bond yield will stay below seven percent near term and not stand in the way of higher corporate profits. Economic data since the September 24 FOMC meeting -- except for the jump in August new home sales -- have leaned toward the view that economic growth is moderating.
"Investors are afraid of being left behind," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker.

Among special situations, Toys R Us rose 2-5/8 to 31-1/2 and Baby Superstore surged five to 24-7/8 after Toys R Us agreed to buy the operator of infant and toddler superstores in a stock deal valued at about $376 million.
AT&T rose 1/2 to 39-3/8 after news it will offer in 40 major markets a new product called AT&T Digital PCS, which combines voice messaging and paging communications in a single telephone.
First USA Inc rallied 2-3/4 to 59-5/8. Merrill Lynch named the stock its Focus One stock of the week.

Among those warning of earnings shortfalls, Great Lakes Chemical lost 3-1/8 to 53-7/8, Engelhard was off 2-7/8 to 20-1/2, Lydall fell 3-3/8 to 21, Restrac tumbled 7-1/2 to 9-1/2, Intelligent Medical slumped 6-3/4 to 7-1/2, Summit Medical was pummeled down 5-3/4 to seven, DSC Communications lost 4-3/8 to 18-3/4, Orthologic shed 4-1/16 to 7-5/16 and Software 2000 lost 2-1/4 to 7-3/4.

But Remedy Corp jumped 8-1/2 to 87 after forecasting third-quarter earnings of about $0.30 a share, exceeding analysts' estimates of $0.24. The client/server support software company also set a two-for-one stock split.
Oakley Inc surged 4-1/4 to 46-1/4. Oppenheimer started coverage with a buy rating.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 14.60 to 1236.11.
The S&P 500 index rose 4.93 to 694.01, a record.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859-1721
